reason: Feasibility is fine: tau is an existing cell-0 knob with a generic --set, exp70b is unchanged when it is off, there is no new code and no runtime change, and 28 Sep W1 slot 3 is free in most branches. The VALUE revision does not hold. (1) The 'no longer a coin flip' premise (b) contradicts the finding's own data. In r19_agg.json, 5 of the 6 6bba tau-added TPs sit at DC >= 0.30 (<0.30: 1 TP / 1 FP / 37 ign; >=0.30: 5 TP / 3 FP). So probe 41's [0.25,0.30) band says nothing about the forks that give the gain. That band evidence is also about symmetric forks that pass tau 0.6; tau adds asymmetric forks. (2) Premise (a) is used one-sidedly. If dc0.30 shows that lab signs do not predict the public sign for division knobs, then the 6bba +0.0043 predicts no better than the 44b6 -0.0013. (3) The only direct public reads of more geometric safe forks are probes 43 and 44 (DC 0.20 / 0.225), and both are null (N4, 0 teams passed). The insertion's +0.001 is a learned-classifier ADD with a different precision profile. (4) The embryo split is robust and follows annotation density: 6bba P(<0) 0.004, 44b6-71 P(<0) 0.99; 6bba 5.2% vs 44b6 0.79% of predicted nodes annotated. The public and private embryos' density is unknown, and the 44b6-71 adds are 0 TP / 4 FP against a precision bar of ~0.265 at J_pub ~0.36. The private sign (71% of the test) is therefore a genuine coin flip. Clip W/L on the lab is 6/16 overall and 6/13 even on 6bba, so the gain rests on 6 lumpy TP events. (5) The action's dummy gate is wrong. tau 0.75 changes num_pred_nodes: +62 nodes on 6bba (12 of 39 clips), +21 on 44b6-17, +92 on 44b6-71 (15 of 71 clips), through the short-track output filter, at a small node-bonus cost. 'Nodes 121,252' would likely FAIL on a correct build, or push someone to explain the difference away. What survives: a user-sanctioned public coin flip with a positive skew (about +0.004 if 6bba-like, about -0.001 if 44b6-like). It is not the 'strongest evidenced' lever, and it has no private case.
